scope: Direct Fast Move reference audio evidence, ownership separation, onset repair, bounded background analysis.

defect.cause: First 200ms of already audible clips used as a silent baseline; threshold exceeded the entire recording.

rules: Use explicit downmix and rate-correct pulse timing; leading clipped sound does not invent an onset.
Compare a 416ms spectral segment against the full local catalogue, both original and background-suppressed spectra. Preserve leaders and competing scores.
A capture cue identifies the requesting HP observation, not acoustic ownership.
Require two distinct reference-aligned occurrences and exactly one legal active side; both active move pools must be known.
Retain mirror/shared-pool and ambiguous observations without forcing ownership.
Deduplicate overlapping recordings with reference alignment and the legal move duration; ignore pre-GO, charged guard intervals, stale appearances and post-result evidence.
Audio-backed identity can refine observed-use duration and energy per observed use; it creates no use or energy on its own.
Timeline measurements and audio references are retained; existing records are not rewritten.

recorded_regression.note: Selected acoustic regressions are not a human-labelled move count or accuracy estimate over all moves.
findings: Two Electrode-section recordings independently match Spark; a simulated Tackle cadence is corrected and subsequent fragmented cadence cannot restore it.
Two overlapping Water Gun recordings align to the same occurrence, not two independent confirmations.
A player-cued clip can contain a clearer opponent sound; end-to-end phone test assigns Spark to the legal opponent.

validation.gradle_final_result: SUCCESS; final invocation up-to-date after all source and test changes

remaining_validation: A fresh live battle is required to measure full HUD identification latency while screen capture and other witnesses compete for resources.
This remains visually cued audio recognition, not a continuous independent fast-move counter.
Catalogue filenames and controlled reference separation do not establish live accuracy for every move. Shared acoustic signatures and mirror ownership can remain unresolved.
